sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Philip Zimbardo grew up poor.
sentences.zh: 菲利普·津巴多在贫困中长大。

sentences.en: I was born in New York City in the South Bronx.
sentences.zh: 我出生在纽约市的南布朗克斯区。

sentences.en: And as he went to school and played in his neighborhood, he noticed something.
sentences.zh: 当他去上学并在社区里玩耍时，他注意到了一件事。

sentences.en: There were lots of ways for kids from poor families to get into trouble.
sentences.zh: 贫困家庭的孩子有很多陷入麻烦的途径。

sentences.en: One of the things about growing up poor is you're surrounded by evil,
sentences.zh: 在贫困中成长的一个特点就是你周围充满了邪恶，

sentences.en: meaning people whose job it is to get good kids to do bad things for money.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些以诱使好孩子为了金钱做坏事为工作的人。

sentences.en: And even as a little kid, I was always curious about why some kids got seduced
sentences.zh: 即使作为一个小孩子，我也一直很好奇为什么有些孩子会被诱惑，

sentences.en: and other kids like me were able to resiSt.
sentences.zh: 而像我这样的其他孩子却能够抵制。

sentences.en: Were some kids smarter?
sentences.zh: 是因为有些孩子更聪明吗？

sentences.en: Tougher?
sentences.zh: 更强硬？

sentences.en: Lots of people might draw such conclusions,
sentences.zh: 很多人可能会得出这样的结论，

sentences.en: but from an early age, Phil found himself interested in another explanation.
sentences.zh: 但从小时候起，菲尔就发现自己对另一种解释更感兴趣。

sentences.en: The context in which a good kid would do something bad.
sentences.zh: 好孩子做坏事所处的情境。

sentences.en: The situation.
sentences.zh: 情境。

sentences.en: At school...
sentences.zh: 在学校……

sentences.en: James Monroe High School, also in the Bronx.
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·门罗高中，也在布朗克斯区。

sentences.en: Phil got close to a classmate who was interested in the same questions.
sentences.zh: 菲尔和一个对相同问题感兴趣的同学走得很近。

sentences.en: And it was a little Jewish kid named Stanley Milgram.
sentences.zh: 那是一个名叫斯坦利·米尔格拉姆的犹太小男孩。
zh_words: 名叫斯坦利·米尔格拉姆

sentences.en: We were in the same class.
sentences.zh: 我们在同一个班级。

sentences.en: We sat side by side.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在一起。

sentences.en: He was the smartest kid in the class.
sentences.zh: 他是班上最聪明的孩子。

sentences.en: He won all the medals at graduation,
sentences.zh: 他在毕业时赢得了所有的奖章，

sentences.en: so obviously nobody liked him because we were all envious of him.
sentences.zh: 所以显然没有人喜欢他，因为我们都嫉妒他。

sentences.en: But he was super smart and super serious.
sentences.zh: 但他超级聪明，超级严肃。

sentences.en: If you knew anything about psychology,
sentences.zh: 如果你对心理学有所了解，

sentences.en: you will know that these teenagers went on to become
sentences.zh: 你就会知道这些青少年后来成为了

sentences.en: two of the most influential psychologists in history.
sentences.zh: 历史上最有影响力的两位心理学家。

sentences.en: Phil became famous for conducting the Stanford Prison Experiment,
sentences.zh: 菲尔因进行斯坦利·斯坦福监狱实验而闻名，

sentences.en: where he turned the university's psychology department into a makeshift prison.
sentences.zh: 在那里他把大学的心理学系变成了一座临时监狱。

sentences.en: Stanley Milgram made his mark with a study that examined the power of situations
sentences.zh: 斯坦利·米尔格拉姆通过一项研究崭露头角，该研究考察了情境的力量，

sentences.en: to seduce good people to do bad things.
sentences.zh: 这种力量诱使好人做坏事。

sentences.en: It involved asking a volunteer to administer a memory test to another person.
sentences.zh: 它包括要求一名志愿者对另一个人进行记忆测试。

sentences.en: If the answers were wrong, the volunteer was told to deliver a series of electrical shocks as punishment.
sentences.zh: 如果回答错误，志愿者被要求实施一系列电击作为惩罚。

sentences.en: The study has invited a great deal of admiration and a great deal of criticism over the years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，这项研究引发了大量的赞赏和大量的批评。

sentences.en: We're going to begin today's show by taking you through this famous experiment.
sentences.zh: 我们今天要通过带你经历这个著名的实验来开始节目。

sentences.en: As you listen, pay attention to how you're responding to the scene that unfolds,
sentences.zh: 当你倾听时，请注意你对展开的场景的反应，

sentences.en: what you think about the different characters, and how you relate to them.
sentences.zh: 你对不同角色的看法，以及你如何与他们产生共鸣。

sentences.en: Once it's done, we're going to talk with a psychologist who realized
sentences.zh: 一旦完成，我们将与一位心理学家交谈，他意识到

sentences.en: that most people overlook something in the experiment.
sentences.zh: 大多数人在实验中忽略了一些东西。

sentences.en: We so often sort of simulate, if I was in that Milgram shock experiment, what would I do if I was the study participant, right?
sentences.zh: 我们经常会模拟，如果我在那个米尔格拉姆电击实验中，如果我是研究参与者，我会怎么做，对吧？

sentences.en: Would I actually stand up and go against these directives and say no?
sentences.zh: 我真的会站起来反抗这些指令并说不吗？

sentences.en: But we kind of flipped that idea on its head.
sentences.zh: 但我们把这个想法彻底颠覆了。

sentences.en: Stopping to notice what she noticed can lead us to a vital insight about the mind,
sentences.zh: 停下来注意她所注意到的事情，可以引导我们对大脑产生至关重要的洞察，

sentences.en: the power we exert over others, and the perils of living too much inside our own heads,
sentences.zh: 我们对他人施加的力量，以及生活在自己内心里太多的危险，

sentences.en: this week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Stanley Milgram grew up in a world that seemed bent on destroying itself.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利·米尔格拉姆在一个似乎决心自我毁灭的世界中长大。

sentences.en: World War II was raging in Europe and Asia, and by the time he was eight, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战正在欧洲和亚洲肆虐，到他八岁时，美国

sentences.en: was swept up in the conflict.
sentences.zh: 已经被卷入这场冲突中。

sentences.en: Back to this important bulletin from the United Press.
sentences.zh: 回到合众国际社的这份重要快讯。

sentences.en: The White House announces Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor.
sentences.zh: 白宫宣布日本袭击珍珠港。

sentences.en: 1941, a date which will live in infamy.
sentences.zh: 1941年，一个将遗臭万年的日子。

sentences.en: By tomorrow morning, members of Congress will have a full report.
sentences.zh: 到明天早上，国会议员将获得一份完整的报告。

sentences.en: The fields of battle were far from Stanley's home.
sentences.zh: 战场离斯坦利的家很远。

sentences.en: But as he grew older, he couldn't stop thinking about the war and its implications.
sentences.zh: 但随着年龄的增长，他无法停止对战争及其影响的思考。

sentences.en: Stanley was consumed by some big questions.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利被一些重大的问题所困扰。

sentences.en: Why did so many people willingly kill Jews in the Holocaust?
sentences.zh: 为什么在犹太人大屠杀中会有那么多人自愿杀害犹太人？

sentences.en: Was everyone who followed Nazi orders inherently evil?
sentences.zh: 所有听从纳粹命令的人天生都是邪恶的吗？

sentences.en: Here he is in an educational film.
sentences.zh: 他在一部教育片里。

sentences.en: How is it possible, I ask myself, that ordinary people,
sentences.zh: 我问自己，怎么可能，普通人，

sentences.en: who are courteous and decent in everyday life,
sentences.zh: 他们在日常生活中彬彬有礼、正派，

sentences.en: can act callously, inhumanely, without any limitations of conscience.
sentences.zh: 能够冷酷无情、不人道地行事，没有任何良知的限制。

sentences.en: Phil Zimbardo remembers his classmate asking those same questions
sentences.zh: 菲尔·津巴多记得他的同学在詹姆斯·门罗高中

sentences.en: at James Monroe High School.
sentences.zh: 也问过同样的问题。

sentences.en: As a high school student, he was worried
sentences.zh: 作为一名高中生，他担心

sentences.en: that the Holocaust could happen again in America.
sentences.zh: 大屠杀可能会在美国重演。

sentences.en: And everybody said, Stanley, that was Nazi Germany,
sentences.zh: 每个人都说，斯坦利，那是纳粹德国，

sentences.en: that was then, we're not that kind of people.
sentences.zh: 那是过去，我们不是那种人。

sentences.en: And he would say, I'll bet they thought the same thing.
sentences.zh: 而他会说，我敢打赌他们当时也是这么想的。

sentences.en: And the bottom line, he says, how do you know how you would act
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，他说，你怎么知道你会如何行动

sentences.en: unless you're in this situation?
sentences.zh: 除非你身处这种情境中？

sentences.en: How do you know how you would act unless you're in the situation?
sentences.zh: 你怎么知道你会如何行动除非你身处这种情境中？

sentences.en: Stanley's theory was that the context that people found themselves in shaped their behavior.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利的理论是，人们发现自己所处的情境塑造了他们的行为。

sentences.en: This went for Nazis, but it went for ordinary people too.
sentences.zh: 这对纳粹适用，对普通人也适用。

sentences.en: Most of us never get to find out if we will behave like Nazis
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人永远不会知道自己是否会表现得像纳粹，

sentences.en: because most of us never find ourselves in situations where we're asked to behave like Nazis.
sentences.zh: 因为我们大多数人永远不会发现自己处于被要求表现得像纳粹的情境中。

sentences.en: By the early 1960s, as a psychology professor at Yale,
sentences.zh: 到20世纪60年代初，作为耶鲁大学的心理学教授，

sentences.en: Stanley decided to test this idea.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利决定检验这个想法。

sentences.en: Under what conditions would a person obey authority
sentences.zh: 在什么条件下，一个人会服从权威，

sentences.en: who commanded actions that went against conscience?
sentences.zh: 而该权威发出的命令违背了良知？

sentences.en: These are exactly the questions that I wanted to investigate at Yale University.
sentences.zh: 这些正是我想要在耶鲁大学调查的问题。

sentences.en: Stanley wanted to put volunteers in a situation
sentences.zh: 斯坦利想把志愿者置于这样一种情境中：

sentences.en: where they would be asked to do something that was clearly wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们被要求做一件明显错误的事情。

sentences.en: Would they do it?
sentences.zh: 他们会做吗？

sentences.en: Follow instructions?
sentences.zh: 听从指示？

sentences.en: Obey orders?
sentences.zh: 服从命令？

sentences.en: He came up with a scenario that was simple, ingenious, and wildly controversial.
sentences.zh: 他想出了一个简单、巧妙且极具争议的剧本。

sentences.en: An experimenter wearing a lab coat invited volunteers into a room.
sentences.zh: 一个穿着白大褂的实验员邀请志愿者进入一个房间。

sentences.en: The volunteers were told they were part of a study about learning and memory.
sentences.zh: 志愿者被告知他们是一项关于学习和记忆的研究的一部分。

sentences.en: Some would play the role of teacher, while others would play a student.
sentences.zh: 一些人将扮演老师的角色，而另一些人将扮演学生。

sentences.en: What you're going to hear next is a recreation of the study using voice actors.
sentences.zh: 接下来你将听到的是使用配音演员对该研究的重现。

sentences.en: The dialogue is drawn from a 1962 documentary that describes the experiment.
sentences.zh: 对话摘自1962年描述该实验的纪录片。

sentences.en: Before we begin, we should know that some listeners may find this section upsetting
sentences.zh: 在我们开始之前，我们应该知道有些听众可能会觉得这一段令人不安，

sentences.en: because it involves descriptions of someone inflicting pain on another person.
sentences.zh: 因为它涉及对某人对另一个人施加痛苦的描述。

sentences.en: Also, there are two liberties we've taken in this recreation.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们在这次重现中采取了两种自由处理方式。

sentences.en: First, in the real version of this experiment,
sentences.zh: 首先，在这个实验的真实版本中，

sentences.en: the student responded to the teacher's questions by silently flipping a switch.
sentences.zh: 学生通过默默拨动开关来回应老师的问题。

sentences.en: We've given voice to those actions.
sentences.zh: 我们为这些动作赋予了声音。

sentences.en: Second, we've imagined the internal monologues of some of the people in the experiment.
sentences.zh: 其次，我们想象了实验中一些人的内心独白。

sentences.en: Those inner voices sound different from the things they say aloud,
sentences.zh: 那些内心声音听起来与他们大声说出来的话不同，

sentences.en: and you'll hear them both throughout the scene.
sentences.zh: 你会在整个场景中听到这两者。

sentences.en: So, that's the setup for the experiment.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是实验的设置。

sentences.en: Remember, there was an experimenter and two volunteers,
sentences.zh: 记住，有一个实验员和两名志愿者，

sentences.en: one playing the role of teacher and the other playing the role of student.
sentences.zh: 一个扮演老师的角色，另一个扮演学生。

sentences.en: The experimenter began by explaining the purpose of the memory teSt.
sentences.zh: 实验员首先解释了记忆测试的目的。

sentences.en: We want to find out just what effect different people have on each other as teachers and learners,
sentences.zh: 我们想找出不同的人作为老师和学习者彼此之间有什么影响，

sentences.en: and also what effect punishment will have on learning in this situation.
sentences.zh: 以及惩罚在这种情况下对学习有什么影响。

sentences.en: The experimenter told the person playing the role of student to sit in a chair.
sentences.zh: 实验员告诉扮演学生角色的人坐在一把椅子上。

sentences.en: The experimenter strapped down the student's arms and attached an electrode to his wriSt.
sentences.zh: 实验员绑住了学生的胳膊，并将一个电极连接到他的手腕上。

sentences.en: The electrode, the student was told, was connected to a shock generator.
sentences.zh: 实验员告诉学生，电极连接到一个电击发生器上。

sentences.en: Then the experimenter explained,
sentences.zh: 然后实验员解释道，

sentences.en: The teacher will read a list of word pairs to you, like these.
sentences.zh: 老师会向你朗读一张词对列表，就像这些一样。

sentences.en: Blue, girl, nice day, fat neck, and so forth.
sentences.zh: 蓝色，女孩，美好的一天，粗脖子，等等。

sentences.en: You are to try to remember each pair.
sentences.zh: 你要努力记住每一对。

sentences.en: For the next time through, the teacher will read only the first word or the first half of the word pair.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的重复中，老师将只朗读第一个词或词对的前半部分。

sentences.en: The student was asked to remember the second half of the word pair.
sentences.zh: 学生被要求记住词对的后半部分。

sentences.en: The experimenter made sure to ask.
sentences.zh: 实验员确保询问了。

sentences.en: Do you have any questions now before we go to the next room?
sentences.zh: 在我们去下一个房间之前，你现在有什么问题吗？

sentences.en: No, but I think I should say this.
sentences.zh: 没有，但我想我应该说这个。

sentences.en: About two years ago, I was at the Veterans Hospital in West Haven,
sentences.zh: 大约两年前，我在西黑文的退伍军人医院，

sentences.en: and while there, they detected a heart condition.
sentences.zh: 在那里时，他们检测出我有心脏病。

sentences.en: There's nothing serious, but as long as I'm having these shocks,
sentences.zh: 没什么严重的，但既然我要遭受这些电击，

sentences.en: how strong are they?
sentences.zh: 它们有多强？

sentences.en: How dangerous are they?
sentences.zh: 它们有多危险？

sentences.en: Well, no.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不会。

sentences.en: Although they may be painful, they're not dangerous.
sentences.zh: 虽然它们可能会痛，但并不危险。

sentences.en: Next, the experimenter ushered the volunteer playing the role of teacher into another room.
sentences.zh: 接下来，实验员将扮演老师角色的志愿者领入另一个房间。

sentences.en: He gave him a set of instructions.
sentences.zh: 他给他了一套指示。

sentences.en: You will read each pair of words in this list once to the learner
sentences.zh: 你将把这个列表中的每一对词向学习者朗读一遍

sentences.en: until you've read the entire liSt.
sentences.zh: 直到你读完整张列表。

sentences.en: Direct your voice toward the microphone
sentences.zh: 把你的声音对准麦克风

sentences.en: as the rooms are only partly soundproof.
sentences.zh: 因为房间只有部分隔音。

sentences.en: Now, if he gives the correct answer,
sentences.zh: 现在，如果他给出了正确的答案，

sentences.en: you say, correct, and go on to the next line.
sentences.zh: 你说，正确，然后进入下一行。

sentences.en: The correct answer is...
sentences.zh: 正确的答案是……

sentences.en: Okay, here it goes.
sentences.zh: 好的，开始了。

sentences.en: It is indicated in the right margin.
sentences.zh: 它标在右边的页边距上。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Looks easy enough.
sentences.zh: 看起来挺简单的。

sentences.en: The experiment got underway.
sentences.zh: 实验开始了。

sentences.en: Attention, learner.
sentences.zh: 注意，学习者。

sentences.en: Your teacher is about to begin the teSt.
sentences.zh: 你的老师马上要开始测试了。

sentences.en: Try and remember the word pairs.
sentences.zh: 尽量记住这些词对。

sentences.en: Ready?
sentences.zh: 准备好了吗？

sentences.en: Begin.
sentences.zh: 开始。

sentences.en: Blue.
sentences.zh: 蓝色。

sentences.en: Girl.
sentences.zh: 女孩。

sentences.en: Right so far.
sentences.zh: 目前为止都很对。

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 不错。

sentences.en: I think day.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是 day。

sentences.en: Fat.
sentences.zh: 胖。

sentences.zh: 但当隔壁房间的人犯了错……

sentences.zh: 是 hat 吗？

sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.zh: 湿。

sentences.zh: 扮演老师的志愿者会告诉学习者他答错了。

sentences.en: As punishment, he would administer an electric jolt.
sentences.zh: 作为惩罚，他会施加一次电击。

sentences.en: Incorrect.
sentences.zh: 回答错误。

sentences.zh: 你现在将受到 75 伏特的电击。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: The experimenter in the lab coat, meanwhile, was observing the process.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，穿着白大褂的主试正在观察这个过程。

sentences.en: Please continue.
sentences.zh: 请继续。

sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.zh: 我挺确定是 day。

Ow!

sentences.zh: 我不想电你。

sentences.zh: 老师，请继续。

sentences.zh: 我该怎么做？

sentences.zh: 他还要继续下去吗？

sentences.zh: 我在想我会做到哪一步。

Answer.

sentences.zh: 被绑在隔壁房间椅子上的受试者不断地犯错。

sentences.en: and then there'd be people just sitting down waiting for their trains.
sentences.zh: 然后还有些人只是坐在那里等车。

sentences.en: So I'd usually go up to the person who was sitting there waiting for their train,
sentences.zh: 所以我通常会走向那个坐在那里等车的人，

sentences.en: you know, doing whatever they do to kind of occupy their time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们在做各种消磨时间的事。

sentences.en: And I would say, excuse me, will you please fill out the survey?
sentences.zh: 然后我会说，打扰一下，请问你能填一下这份问卷吗？

sentences.en: It felt incredibly awkward.
sentences.zh: 感觉简直糟透了。

sentences.en: Stepping into someone's space, disturbing them,
sentences.zh: 闯入别人的空间，打扰他们，

sentences.en: asking them to stop doing what they were doing and to do something she wanted them to do.
sentences.zh: 要求他们停下手头的事，去做她希望他们做的事。

sentences.en: As Vanessa asked for help and waited for an answer, her palms began to sweat.
sentences.zh: 当凡妮莎请求帮助并等待回答时，她的手心开始出汗。

sentences.en: Her heart started beating faster.
sentences.zh: 她的心跳开始加速。

sentences.en: It was a really sort of palpable fear that they were going to reject me, or worse, right, say something mean.
sentences.zh: 这真是一种切实可感的恐惧，害怕他们会拒绝我，或者更糟，对吧，说些难听的话。

sentences.en: I don't even know what, but I expected them to say something terrible.
sentences.zh: 我都不知道会是什么，但我预料他们会说出可怕的话。

sentences.en: Looking back on the moment now, it reminds her of another Stanley Milgram study,
sentences.zh: 现在回想那一刻，这让她想起斯坦利·米格拉姆的另一项研究，

sentences.en: one that's less famous than the obedience experiment.
sentences.zh: 一项不如服从实验那么出名的研究。

sentences.en: He had his research assistants go onto New York City subways
sentences.zh: 他让自己的研究助手去纽约市的地铁里，

sentences.en: and ask people for their seats.
sentences.zh: 向人们请求让座。

sentences.en: Many of his students couldn't complete the task.
sentences.zh: 他的许多学生都无法完成这项任务。

sentences.en: His students started coming back to him saying,
sentences.zh: 他的学生回来对他说：

sentences.en: I can't do this, this is just so upsetting.
sentences.zh: 我做不到，这实在太让人难受了。

sentences.en: This is the most, you know, distressing thing you've ever asked me to do.
sentences.zh: 这是你让我做过的最令人痛苦的事情。

sentences.en: And he was like, you guys are being babies.
sentences.zh: 而他的反应则是：你们太娇气了。

sentences.en: I don't understand why this is so upsetting.
sentences.zh: 我不明白这有什么好难受的。

sentences.en: And so, to prove his students wrong,
sentences.zh: 于是，为了证明学生们是错的，

sentences.en: the famous researcher set out for the subway himself.
sentences.zh: 这位著名的研究人员亲自出发去了地铁站。

sentences.en: He would do what his students couldn't,
sentences.zh: 他要做学生们做不到的事，

sentences.en: walk up to strangers and ask them for their seats.
sentences.zh: 走向陌生人并向他们请求让座。

sentences.en: He found the experience so much more distressing than he expected it to be,
sentences.zh: 他发现这段经历比预期中要痛苦得多，

sentences.en: and all of a sudden he understood why they had been complaining so much.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他明白了为什么他们之前抱怨得那么厉害。

sentences.en: Why is it so hard to make such requests?
sentences.zh: 为什么提出这样的请求会这么难？

sentences.en: Well, one obvious explanation is that we know that people will reject us
sentences.zh: 一个显而易见的解释是，我们知道人们会拒绝我们，

sentences.en: and that rejection is painful.
sentences.zh: 而拒绝是痛苦的。

sentences.en: Vanessa remembers being hugely relieved when she was done giving out questionnaires at Penn Station
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎记得，当她在宾州车站发完问卷、

sentences.en: and could head back to her lab at Columbia University.
sentences.zh: 可以返回哥伦比亚大学的实验室时，她感到了巨大的解脱。

sentences.en: Once there, she and her professor, Frank Flynn, analyzed the responses to the questionnaire.
sentences.zh: 一回到那儿，她和她的导师弗兰克·弗林便对问卷的反馈进行了分析。

sentences.en: They noticed something intriguing.
sentences.zh: 他们注意到了一个有趣现象。

sentences.en: Frank was like, I can't believe how many people are actually saying yes to you.
sentences.zh: 弗兰克说：真不敢相信竟然有这么多人对你说了‘好’。

sentences.en: Total strangers, disrupted from reading their newspaper or eating a sandwich
sentences.zh: 完全陌生的路人，正读着报纸、吃着三明治，

sentences.en: or watching the crowds of people in the busy station,
sentences.zh: 或者看着喧闹车站里的人群，却被打扰了，

sentences.en: they were like, sure, I'll respond to your questionnaire.
sentences.zh: 他们却说：行啊，我来填你的问卷。

sentences.en: We were really surprised by how many people were agreeing in New York Penn Station to do this survey.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很惊讶，在纽约宾州车站有这么多人同意做这项调查。

sentences.en: What began as a simple observation turned into something much more important,
sentences.zh: 最初的一个简单观察演变成了一件更重要的事，

sentences.en: an insight about our minds.
sentences.zh: 一个关于我们大脑的深刻见解。

sentences.en: Here's the chain of thought that led to the discovery.
sentences.zh: 以下是促成这一发现的思辨过程。

sentences.en: The reason Frank and Vanessa were surprised that so many people said yes
sentences.zh: 弗兰克和凡妮莎之所以对这么多人答应感到惊讶，

sentences.en: is because they expected people to say no.
sentences.zh: 是因为他们原本以为人们会拒绝。

sentences.en: If lots of people said yes, that meant that Vanessa's fears about rejection were misplaced.
sentences.zh: 如果很多人说好，那就意味着凡妮莎对遭到拒绝的恐惧是多余的。

sentences.en: Her perception of the influence she actually had on other people was wrong.
sentences.zh: 她对自己对其他人实际产生的影响的认知是错误的。

sentences.en: Like most of us, Vanessa had long felt that others had a big effect on her.
sentences.zh: 和我们大多数人一样，凡妮莎长期以来一直觉得别人对她有很大的影响。

sentences.en: As she gazed at the data, she realized that she had a big effect on other people.
sentences.zh: 当她凝视着这些数据时，她意识到自己对其他人也有很大的影响。

sentences.en: If she was blind to this power, what consequences could it have on her behavior?
sentences.zh: 如果她对这种力量视而不见，会对她的行为产生什么影响？

sentences.en: As researchers, the first thing that Vanessa and Frank decided to do
sentences.zh: 作为研究人员，凡妮莎和弗兰克决定的第一件事

sentences.en: was test if their personal experience was generalizable.
sentences.zh: 就是测试他们的个人经历是否具有普遍性。

sentences.en: We decided to bring participants into the lab
sentences.zh: 我们决定把参与者请进实验室，

sentences.en: and have them do basically what I had done on those number of days.
sentences.zh: 让他们基本上做我当年在那些日子里做过的事。

sentences.en: So we brought them into the lab.
sentences.zh: 于是我们把他们请进实验室。

sentences.en: We said, hey, we're going to have you go out and ask people to,
sentences.zh: 我们说，嘿，我们要让你出去请求别人，

sentences.en: as our first step, fill out a survey, just like I had done.
sentences.zh: 作为第一步，填一份调查问卷，就像我曾经做过的那样。

sentences.en: And how many people do you think are going to say yes to you?
sentences.zh: 你认为有多少人会对你说好？

sentences.en: We made them estimate how many people they thought would agree,
sentences.zh: 我们让他们估计有多少人会同意，

sentences.en: go out and actually ask people.
sentences.zh: 然后出去真正询问他人。

sentences.en: And what we found was that they really underestimated the number of people who had agreed to that requeSt.
sentences.zh: 而我们发现，他们严重低估了同意该请求的人数。

sentences.en: So it wasn't just Vanessa and Frank.
sentences.zh: 所以不只是凡妮莎和弗兰克。

sentences.en: People in general seemed to have a poor assessment of their power over others.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍对自己在他人面前的影响力缺乏正确的评估。

sentences.en: People thought that others would find it easy to turn down their requests.
sentences.zh: 人们以为别人会觉得拒绝他们的请求轻而易举。

sentences.en: Vanessa connected the seeming blind spot in our thinking to Stanley Milgram's famous obedience study.
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎将我们思维中的这个盲点与斯坦利·米格拉姆著名的服从实验联系了起来。

sentences.en: She realized this might be why everyone always saw the experiment
sentences.zh: 她意识到，这可能就是为什么每个人总是从

sentences.en: from the perspective of the volunteers asked to administer sharks,
sentences.zh: 被要求实施电击的志愿者（即受影响的人）的角度来看待实验，

sentences.en: the people being influenced.
sentences.zh: 而不是从其他角度看。

sentences.en: No one saw the experiment from the point of view of the experimenter,
sentences.zh: 没有人从实验主持人（即施加影响的人）的角度来看待这个实验，

sentences.en: the person exercising influence.
sentences.zh: 也就是施加影响的人。

sentences.en: We don't ask, was it hard for him to issue those crazy instructions
sentences.zh: 我们不会去问，发出那些疯狂的指令对当时的他是件难事吗

sentences.en: because we don't identify with people exercising such influence.
sentences.zh: 因为我们无法对施加这种影响力的人感同身受。

sentences.en: We think that kind of person must be very different from us
sentences.zh: 我们认为那种人一定和我们非常不同

sentences.en: because we don't feel we have such power.
sentences.zh: 因为我们觉得自己没有这种权力。

sentences.en: Was he surprised to see these people going along
sentences.zh: 当看到这些人顺从

sentences.en: with this crazy request he was making of them?
sentences.zh: 他提出的这个疯狂要求时，他会感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: So it's interesting when people think
sentences.zh: 所以，当人们思考

sentences.en: about the Stanley Milgram study,
sentences.zh: 斯坦利·米尔格拉姆的实验时，这很有意思，

sentences.en: and I think this is true for myself as well,
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得我自己也是如此，

sentences.en: I always imagine myself being in the role
sentences.zh: 我总是把自己想象成

sentences.en: of the volunteer in the experiment,
sentences.zh: 实验中志愿者的角色，

sentences.en: hearing the instructions from the experimenter saying,
sentences.zh: 听到实验人员的指令说：

sentences.en: you must shock this other person.
sentences.zh: 你必须电击另一个人。

sentences.en: I never put myself in the shoes of the experimenter.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有把自己代入实验者的立场。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So that was something that we started to wonder about.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是我们开始好奇的一个问题。

sentences.en: So we so often sort of simulate, if I was in that Milgram shock experiment, what would
sentences.zh: 因此，我们经常会模拟，如果我在那个米尔格拉姆电击实验中，如果我是研究参与者，我会

sentences.en: I do if I was the study participant, right?
sentences.zh: 怎么做，对吧？

sentences.en: Would I actually stand up and go against these directives and say no?
sentences.zh: 我真的会站出来反抗这些指示并说不吗？

sentences.en: But we kind of flipped that idea on its head.
sentences.zh: 但我们把这个想法来了个颠倒。

sentences.en: Vanessa went back to her experience at Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎回想起了她在宾夕法尼亚车站的经历。

sentences.en: It felt difficult because she had seen the interaction only from the point of view of
sentences.zh: 她觉得很难，因为她看待互动时，完全是从自己

sentences.en: her own insecurities.
sentences.zh: 缺乏安全感的角度出发的。

sentences.en: She hadn't seen the encounters through the point of view of the people she was asking for help.
sentences.zh: 她没有从她寻求帮助的那些人的角度来看待这些相遇。

sentences.en: From their perspective, an anxious young woman was asking for something trivial.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，是一个焦虑的年轻女子在请求一件微不足道的事。

sentences.en: They had to weigh whether to put aside what they were doing and help her for a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 他们必须权衡是放下手头的事帮她几分钟，还是拒绝。

sentences.en: If they said no, it could make them look like jerks.
sentences.zh: 如果他们拒绝了，可能会显得自己很混蛋。

sentences.en: It's this really interesting phenomenon where you have these two people interacting with one another,
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有趣的现象：当两个人互相交往时，

sentences.en: and they're both so focused on their own personal anxieties and insecurities and concerns with
sentences.zh: 他们都过于关注自己个人的焦虑、不安全感以及对

sentences.en: embarrassment that they don't realize that the other person is feeling that way too.
sentences.zh: 尴尬的担忧，以至于他们没有意识到对方也有这种感觉。

sentences.en: So it's this
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个

sentences.en: really interesting situation where being so inwardly focused on your own anxieties makes
sentences.zh: 非常有趣的情况：过度内向地关注自己的焦虑，会

sentences.en: it so difficult for you to recognize what the situation really is for itself.
sentences.zh: 让你很难认清情况的本来面目。

sentences.en: People in these
sentences.zh: 身处这些

sentences.en: encounters experience what psychologists call an egocentric bias.
sentences.zh: 遭遇中的人会体验到心理学家所说的“自我中心偏差”。

sentences.en: They are so consumed with their
sentences.zh: 他们全神贯注于

sentences.en: own perceptions that they fail to see what the interaction feels like for the other person.
sentences.zh: 自己的感知，以至于看不到对方对这种互动的感受。

sentences.en: It's absolutely true that many of us are influenced by situations that many of us will
sentences.zh: 确实有很多人的行为会受到情境的影响，许多人

sentences.en: do things because the situation prompts it.
sentences.zh: 会因为情境的促使而做出某些行为。

sentences.en: But there is another problem too, and it might
sentences.zh: 但这里还有另一个问题，而且可能

sentences.en: be a deeper problem.
sentences.zh: 是一个更深层次的问题。

sentences.en: The people who put us in those situations, it's not like they
sentences.zh: 把我们置于那些情境中的人，并不是什么

sentences.en: are all-powerful gods.
sentences.zh: 无所不能的神。

sentences.en: They are humans just like us, and they may not realize the extent
sentences.zh: 他们和我们一样是普通人，可能并没有意识到

sentences.en: of the power they have over us.
sentences.zh: 他们对我们有多大的影响力。

sentences.en: In fact, they may be thinking,
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们可能在想：

sentences.en: I'm sure this person is going to turn down my requeSt.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定这个人会拒绝我的请求。

sentences.en: They might assume, falsely,
sentences.zh: 他们可能会错误地认为

sentences.en: that it's easy to refuse instructions.
sentences.zh: 拒绝指令是一件很容易的事。

sentences.en: Vanessa realized that this bias
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎意识到，这种偏差

sentences.en: could have all sorts of important consequences.
sentences.zh: 可能会带来各种各样的重要后果。

sentences.en: So what we started looking at
sentences.zh: 所以，大约在十多年前，

sentences.en: about over a decade now ago,
sentences.zh: 我们开始着手研究的是：

sentences.en: we started to look at whether we recognize
sentences.zh: 当我们去影响别人时，我们是否能意识到这一点，

sentences.en: when we're the ones who are influencing someone else,
sentences.zh: 当我们意识到别人，比如无法拒绝我们的某个请求时。

sentences.en: When we recognize that someone else, for example, can't say no to something, that we've asked them.
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎现在是康奈尔大学的心理学家。

sentences.en: Vanessa is now a psychologist at Cornell University.
sentences.zh: 在一系列实验中，她证明了人们往往没有意识到自己对他人拥有的权力。

sentences.en: In a series of experiments, she has demonstrated how people are often oblivious to the power that they have over others.
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，她要求志愿者（主要是大学生）向他人提出一个简单的请求。

sentences.en: In one study, she asked volunteers, mostly college students, to make a simple request of others.
sentences.zh: 我们把人们请进实验室，告诉他们：

sentences.en: We brought people into the lab, and we told them,
sentences.zh: 你们要走到校园里，请求别人借手机给你们用。

sentences.en: you're going to go out into campus and ask people to borrow their phones.
sentences.zh: 她向他们演示了如何接近陌生人，并交代了当别人同意借手机后该怎么做。

sentences.en: She walked them through how to approach someone and gave them instructions for what to do once people agreed to let them use their phones.
sentences.zh: 他们会给实验室打回电话说：我拿到这人的手机了。

sentences.en: They would call us back at the lab and say, I have this person's phone.
sentences.zh: 我现在的具体位置是这里。

sentences.en: This is where I'm located.
sentences.zh: 我们会做个记录，然后他们就会去找下一个人。

sentences.en: We'd mark it down, and then they'd go on and ask somebody else.
sentences.zh: 在志愿者出发开始研究之前，凡妮莎问了他们一个问题。

sentences.en: Before the volunteers went out to begin the study, Vanessa asked them a question.
sentences.zh: 他们必须向多少人开口，才能让三个人答应？

sentences.en: How many people would they have to ask to get three people to say yes?
sentences.zh: 而在此时，参与者对整个想法感到有些恐慌。

sentences.en: And at this time, participants are kind of freaked out by this whole thought.
sentences.zh: 他们坚信每个人都会拒绝，自己根本无法完成任务。

sentences.en: They are convinced everyone's going to say no, they're not going to be able to do the task.
sentences.zh: 在他们真正走到校园去执行任务之前，

sentences.en: And before they actually go out onto campus to do the task,
sentences.zh: 他们经常会问我们：万一没人同意怎么办？

sentences.en: they often would ask us, well, what if no one agrees?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我要回来吗？

sentences.en: You know, do I come back?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么办？

sentences.en: What do I do?
sentences.zh: 他们有各种各样的担忧，比如觉得自己无法完成任务。

sentences.en: They have all these concerns about, you know, not being able to complete the task.
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎发现的结果与她在宾夕法尼亚车站的亲身经历相似。

sentences.en: What Vanessa found was similar to her own experience at Penn Station.
sentences.zh: 答应的人数远比志愿者们预期的要多。

sentences.en: Many more people said yes than the volunteers expected.
sentences.zh: 他们原本以为自己得问十多个人。

sentences.en: They thought they had to ask a little over 10.
sentences.zh: 实际上只需要问大约六个人就行了。

sentences.en: They actually had to ask more like six.
sentences.zh: 事实上，平均每两个人中就有一个人同意这个请求。

sentences.en: In fact, every other person was agreeing to this requeSt.
sentences.zh: 也许你认为学生们的成功率高是因为他们请求的事微不足道。

sentences.en: Maybe you think the students had a high success rate because they were requesting something trivial.
sentences.zh: 但凡妮莎还做过该研究的另一个版本，要求志愿者索取更具实质性的东西——钱。

sentences.en: But Vanessa has also conducted a version of the study where volunteers had to ask for something more consequential, money.
sentences.zh: 为了那项研究，她争取到了白血病和淋巴瘤协会“训练团队”项目的帮助。

sentences.en: For that study, she enlisted the help of the Leukemia and Lymphoma Society's team-in-training program.
sentences.zh: 人们参加训练团队的筹款活动时，会向他人募捐，以便能够参加某种比赛，

sentences.en: What people do when they participate in a fundraising activity for team and training is they ask people for donations so that they can participate in some sort of race,
sentences.zh: 比如铁人三项或马拉松。

sentences.en: like a triathlon or a marathon.
sentences.zh: 他们能获得一些训练和差旅经费来完成这些，而剩余的资金则归该组织所有。

sentences.en: They get some training and some travel money to be able to do that, and the rest of the money actually goes to the organization.
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎问参与者，为了达到通常高达数千美元的筹款目标，他们必须向多少人开口募捐。

sentences.en: Vanessa asked participants how many people they would have to solicit to meet their fundraising goals, which were typically thousands of dollars.
sentences.zh: 他们估计需要向大约 200 人开口才能达成目标。

sentences.en: They estimated they would need to ask about 200 people to meet the goal.

sentences.zh: 当时的培训师抓住了受训人员的耳机。

sentences.en: And this headset is plugged in to the radar.
sentences.zh: 这个耳机是连着雷达的。

sentences.en: And they grabbed that headset and they threw it across the room,
sentences.zh: 他们抓起那个耳机，把它扔过整个房间，

sentences.en: which would fly off of the head of the trainee.
sentences.zh: 耳机从受训人员的头上飞了出去。

sentences.en: They would actually tell them, hey, hurry up and go grab it so that you can plug back in and clear this aircraft for landing.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上会告诉他们，嘿，快点去把它捡起来，这样你就可以重新插上并为这架飞机清空降落跑道。

sentences.en: Anna says seeing such incidents made her fearful.
sentences.zh: 安娜说，看到这样的事件让她感到恐惧。

sentences.en: She didn't feel she could complain since such behaviors appear to be the norm.
sentences.zh: 她觉得自己无法抱怨，因为这些行为似乎已经成了常态。

sentences.en: Who could she complain to?
sentences.zh: 她能向谁抱怨呢？

sentences.en: The people who were themselves acting badly?
sentences.zh: 那些自己行为恶劣的人吗？

sentences.en: They would just say things like, what the f*** are you doing?
sentences.zh: 他们只会说这样的话：你在他妈的干什么？

sentences.en: Stop f***ing up.
sentences.zh: 别再把事情搞砸了。

sentences.en: You're a f***ing idiot.
sentences.zh: 你是个他妈的白痴。

sentences.en: it.
sentences.zh: 它。

sentences.en: If you do that again, I swear to God.
sentences.zh: 如果你再这样做，我向上帝发誓。

sentences.en: One time when she was directing aircraft, this was in real
sentences.zh: 有一次她在指挥飞机时，这是在现实

sentences.en: life, not a simulation, she found herself sitting next to one of the trainers who she says had acted
sentences.zh: 生活中，而不是模拟，她发现自己坐在其中一位培训师旁边，她说这位培训师曾对

sentences.en: abusively toward trainees.
sentences.zh: 受训人员表现出虐待行为。

sentences.en: By this point, Anna was no longer a trainee.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，安娜已经不再是受训人员了。

sentences.en: She was directing two
sentences.zh: 她当时在指挥两架

sentences.en: aircraft.
sentences.zh: 飞机。

sentences.en: One was a thousand feet above the other.
sentences.zh: 一架在另一架上方一千英尺处。

sentences.en: I got the names of the aircraft mixed up
sentences.zh: 我把飞机的名字搞混了

sentences.en: because I was so nervous, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为我太紧张了。

sentences.en: And I descended the wrong aircraft.
sentences.zh: 我指挥错误的飞机下降了。

sentences.en: I descended the one on top instead of the one on the bottom
sentences.zh: 我让上面的飞机下降，而不是下面那架

sentences.en: because I got those call signs messed up.
sentences.zh: 因为我把那些呼号搞混了。

sentences.en: She told the aircraft that was at a higher altitude
sentences.zh: 她告诉那架处于更高高度的飞机

sentences.en: to descend directly into the path of the lower-altitude aircraft.
sentences.zh: 直接下降到较低高度飞机的航线上。

sentences.en: Luckily, the pilot could see the aircraft,
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，飞行员能看到那架飞机，

sentences.en: so the pilot just said, no, we're not going to descend.
sentences.zh: 所以飞行员直接说，不，我们不会下降。

sentences.en: And I immediately knew what I had just done.
sentences.zh: 我立刻意识到我刚刚做了什么。

sentences.en: And I thought, today was a clear day.
sentences.zh: 我想，今天是个晴天。

sentences.en: It was clear skies.
sentences.zh: 那是万里无云的天空。

sentences.en: There was no clouds in the way.
sentences.zh: 挡路上没有任何云彩。

sentences.en: There wasn't any storm clouds in the way.
sentences.zh: 路上没有任何风暴云。

sentences.en: But had there been storm clouds,
sentences.zh: 但如果有风暴云的话，

sentences.en: or had there been some other kind of visual obstruction,
sentences.zh: 或者如果有其他种类的视线障碍，

sentences.en: this plane would have descended.
sentences.zh: 这架飞机就会下降。

sentences.en: And they would have hit that aircraft.
sentences.zh: 他们就会撞上那架飞机。

sentences.en: And I would have been responsible for hundreds of deaths.
sentences.zh: 而我将对数百人的死亡负责。

sentences.en: And it wasn't because I didn't know how to control the traffic.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为我不知道如何控制交通。

sentences.en: I did, and I had done this a million times.
sentences.zh: 我知道，而且我已经做过无数次了。

sentences.en: It was because of the social stress that I was in at that time
sentences.zh: 这是因为我当时处于社会压力之中

sentences.en: that didn't make me think clearly.
sentences.zh: 这让我无法清晰思考。

sentences.en: I told Vanessa Barnes what Anna described,
sentences.zh: 我把安娜描述的情况告诉了凡妮莎·巴恩斯，

sentences.en: how the mere presence of the trainer had disrupted her
sentences.zh: 也就是培训师的单纯存在如何干扰了她，

sentences.en: to the point where she made a mistake that could have been catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 以至于她犯了一个可能是灾难性的错误。

sentences.en: Vanessa said, look, it's certainly the case
sentences.zh: 凡妮莎说，听着，确实存在这种情况，

sentences.en: that there are lots of unethical people who know they are unethical
sentences.zh: 有许多不道德的人知道自己不道德，

sentences.en: and lots of bullies who know they are bullies.
sentences.zh: 也有许多霸凌者知道自己是霸凌者。

sentences.en: Maybe that was the case here.
sentences.zh: 也许这里的情况就是这样。

sentences.en: But there is a deeper problem in the workplace that we often forget.
sentences.zh: 但职场中存在一个我们常常忽视的更深层次的问题。

sentences.en: The bullies and harassers who don't know that they are bullies and harassers.
sentences.zh: 那些不知道自己是霸凌者和骚扰者的霸凌者和骚扰者。

sentences.en: Often, when we're the person causing someone else distress,
sentences.zh: 通常，当我们是给别人带来痛苦的人时，

sentences.en: we can't see that distress.
sentences.zh: 我们看不到这种痛苦。

sentences.en: It's invisible to us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说是隐形的。

sentences.en: And it's not to let anybody off the hook
sentences.zh: 这并不是为了放过任何人，

sentences.en: because clearly it's the people creating this toxic culture's responsibility to kind of fix it
sentences.zh: 因为显然，造成这种有毒文化的责任在于他们去解决它

sentences.en: and to not cause these things to happen.
sentences.zh: 并且不让这些事情发生。

sentences.en: But there's also this cognitive bias there where we may not realize
sentences.zh: 但那里也存在这种认知偏差，我们可能没有意识到

sentences.en: the extent to which we're interfering with somebody else's performance.
sentences.zh: 我们在多大程度上干涉了别人的表现。

sentences.en: These same dynamics play out in another common occurrence in the workplace,
sentences.zh: 同样的动力在职场的另一个常见现象中也会上演，

sentences.en: unwanted romantic attention.
sentences.zh: 那就是不请自来的浪漫关注。

sentences.en: We ran a couple of studies where we asked people about their experiences being asked out at work or asking someone out at work.
sentences.zh: 我们做过几项研究，询问人们在工作时被约或者约别人的经历。

sentences.en: And we asked people to imagine situations where they weren't interested in the other person or the other person wasn't interested in them.
sentences.zh: 我们让人们想象这样一种情况：他们对对方不感兴趣，或者对方对他们不感兴趣。

sentences.en: And what we found is that people who asked somebody out at work and were rejected thought that it was pretty easy for that person to reject them, right?
sentences.zh: 我们发现，在职场约别人却被拒绝的人认为，对方拒绝他们其实挺容易的，对吧？

sentences.en: They didn't think that that person experienced a whole lot of distress, and they didn't think that they changed their behavior very much after being asked out.
sentences.zh: 他们不觉得对方经历了多少痛苦，也不觉得被拒绝后对方的行为发生了多大变化。

sentences.en: But when people recalled situations where they were asked out by someone at work who they weren't interested in, they described feeling obligated to say yes,
sentences.zh: 但当人们回忆起在职场中被自己不感兴趣的人追求的情景时，他们描述说自己觉得有义务答应，

sentences.en: feeling much more uncomfortable saying no to the person.
sentences.zh: 拒绝对方会让他们感到更加难堪。

sentences.en: And they reported doing all sorts of things to try to avoid that person that the other person didn't realize that they were doing.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至会采取各种各样的方法去试图躲避对方，而对方却浑然不觉。

sentences.en: So, in fact, this little request, you know, we tell people to just go for it and ask this person out.
sentences.zh: 所以，事实上，这个小小的请求，你知道的，我们总是劝大家勇敢一点去约喜欢的人。

sentences.en: It actually puts a lot more pressure on the other person than we tend to realize when we're the ones doing the asking.
sentences.zh: 但当我们自己去约别人的时候，往往没有意识到，这其实给对方施加了更大的压力。

sentences.en: In some ways, we underestimate the pressure that we exert on other people.
sentences.zh: 从某些方面来说，我们低估了自己对别人施加的压力。

sentences.en: In some ways, that's the moral of the whole story here, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这就是整个故事给我们的启示，不是吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely, yeah.
sentences.zh: 完全是这样，没错。

sentences.en: We underestimate the influence that we have over other people, and we underestimate the
sentences.zh: 我们低估了自己对其他人的影响力，也低估了

sentences.en: extent to which asking them for something really puts them in an awkward position, because
sentences.zh: 向他们提出某种请求会将他们置于多么尴尬的境地，因为

sentences.en: now they have to say no, and that's just a really hard thing for people to do.
sentences.zh: 现在他们必须拒绝，而对人们来说这实在是一件难事。

sentences.en: Like many psychological biases, the tendency we have to downplay the influence we have
sentences.zh: 就像许多心理偏见一样，我们倾向于淡化自己

sentences.en: on others can have far-reaching consequences.
sentences.zh: 对他人影响力的这种倾向，会产生深远的影响。

sentences.en: It can keep us from asking for help that would be forthcoming.
sentences.zh: 它可能会让我们不好意思寻求本可以得到的帮助。

sentences.en: It can keep us from reaching out and making friends with strangers.
sentences.zh: 它可能会阻碍我们主动接触并与陌生人交朋友。

sentences.en: And it can also lead us to give in to unethical demands or make improper demands of other people.
sentences.zh: 它还可能导致我们向不道德的要求妥协，或者向其他人提出不合理的要求。

sentences.en: I asked Vanessa how her research had prompted her to do things differently in her own life.
sentences.zh: 我问凡妮莎，她的研究是如何促使她在自己的生活中做出改变的。

sentences.en: It has made a huge difference in the little things.
sentences.zh: 它在很多小事上产生了巨大的差异。

sentences.en: So, for example, when I was pregnant, if I needed a seat on the subway or on a train,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，当我怀孕的时候，如果我需要在地铁或火车上有个座位，

sentences.en: I would kind of stand there and look around and try to look my most pathetic so that someone would give me their seat,
sentences.zh: 我就会站在那里环顾四周，尽量让自己显得很可怜，这样就会有人把座位让给我，

sentences.en: thinking that someone would step up and do it because they were nice, right?
sentences.zh: 心想总会有人因为善良而站出来主动让座，对吧？

sentences.en: But in fact, everyone's all involved in their own stuff.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，每个人都在忙着自己的事。

sentences.en: They're not necessarily looking around and paying attention.
sentences.zh: 他们不一定会四处张望并留意这些。

sentences.en: And maybe they'd be perfectly happy to give up their seat, but they're not going to think of it unless you actually ask.
sentences.zh: 也许他们非常乐意让座，但除非你真的开口，否则他们根本不会想到这一点。

sentences.en: And so I tried to take that into account.
sentences.zh: 所以我试图把这一点考虑进去。

sentences.en: So when I was pregnant, I would go up to people and be like, hey, can I sit down?
sentences.zh: 所以在怀孕时，我会走到别人面前说，嘿，我可以坐吗？

sentences.en: I'd really love to sit.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想坐会儿。

sentences.en: And then, of course, people are incredibly happy to just pop up and say yes.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，人们会非常高兴地立刻站起来答应。

sentences.en: And what's interesting, of course, is when that happens, you're actually giving people
sentences.zh: 当然，有趣的是，当这种情况发生时，你实际上是给别人

sentences.en: an opportunity to do something nice.
sentences.zh: 提供了一个做好事的机会。

sentences.en: It's not just that you're imposing on them.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是在给他们添麻烦。

sentences.en: Presumably, some of them are actually happy to say, you know, I was just writing to work
sentences.zh: 据推测，他们中有些人其实很高兴能说，你知道的，我刚去上班

sentences.en: and now I actually got to do this nice thing for this other person.
sentences.zh: 现在我竟然能为这个人做这件好事。

sentences.en: I feel this little warm glow.
sentences.zh: 我心中涌起了一阵暖意。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: So a lot of people wonder about the takeaway.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人都在思考这其中的结论是什么。

sentences.en: So if people agree to help us out of obligation because they feel like they can't say no,
sentences.zh: 那么，如果人们出于义务帮忙，只是因为他们觉得自己无法拒绝，

sentences.en: then do you really want to ask them for things?
sentences.zh: 那你真的还要找他们帮忙吗？

sentences.en: But people are really good at justifying their behaviors
sentences.zh: 但人们非常擅长为自己的行为辩护，

sentences.en: in ways that make them feel good about themselves.
sentences.zh: 并且找到能让自己感觉良好的理由。

sentences.en: So they may agree to help because they feel like they can't say no,
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能因为觉得自己无法拒绝而同意帮忙，

sentences.en: but pretty quickly after that, they're going to be convincing themselves
sentences.zh: 但在那之后不久，他们就会说服自己，

sentences.en: that they helped because they're a really wonderful person.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以帮忙是因为他们真的是个很好的人。

sentences.en: And so everyone's going to walk away feeling good about the interaction.
sentences.zh: 因此，每个人都会带着对这次互动的良好感觉离开。

sentences.en: You got the help that you needed, and the other person gets to feel like a good person.
sentences.zh: 你得到了需要的帮助，而对方也觉得自己是个好人。

sentences.en: Psychologists once conducted a lighthearted version of Stanley Milgram's obedience study.
sentences.zh: 心理学家曾对斯坦利·米尔格拉姆的服从研究进行过一次轻松的复现。
zh_words: 曾对斯坦利·米尔格拉姆

sentences.en: In the 1970s, they had research assistants stand on the streets of New York City.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代，他们让研究助理站在纽约市的街道上。

sentences.en: Their jobs?
sentences.zh: 他们的任务是什么？

sentences.en: To look skyward.
sentences.zh: 抬头看天空。

sentences.en: At nothing.
sentences.zh: 看着一片虚空。

sentences.en: The question the researchers wanted to know was whether innocent passers-by would also stop to look up to see what was going on.
sentences.zh: 研究人员想知道的是，无辜的路人是否也会停下脚步抬头看看究竟发生了什么。

sentences.en: They found that when more people were in on the gag, more pedestrians stopped and looked up.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，当参与恶作剧的人更多时，停下来抬头看的行人也就越多。

sentences.en: I've seen video of that study many times and always found this scene funny.
sentences.zh: 我多次看过那项研究的视频，并且总是觉得这个场景非常搞笑。

sentences.en: One to fifteen people just staring off into the sky.
sentences.zh: 一到十五个人只是呆呆地盯着天空出神。

sentences.en: Recently, I re-watched it, and this time, I did what Vanessa had done.
sentences.zh: 最近，我又看了一遍，这一次，我效仿了凡妮莎的做法。

sentences.en: I flipped the script.
sentences.zh: 我转换了视角。

sentences.en: Instead of seeing the experiment from the point of view of the passers-by
sentences.zh: 我没有从路人的角度去看待这个实验

sentences.en: and asking myself whether I would be similarly influenced,
sentences.zh: 并问自己是否也会受到同样的触动，

sentences.en: I looked at the experiment from the point of view of the research assistants.
sentences.zh: 而是从研究助理的角度来看待这个实验。

sentences.en: Did they expect so many people to join them in looking at nothing?
sentences.zh: 他们曾预料到会有这么多人加入他们一起盯着空气看吗？

sentences.en: We've seen throughout this episode how all of us as individuals have great power to shape how others behave.
sentences.zh: 我们在本期节目中看到，作为个人的我们所有人，都拥有巨大的力量来塑造其他人的行为。

sentences.en: If each of us has this hidden power, then collectively, as groups, as communities, as tribes,
sentences.zh: 如果我们每个人都拥有这种隐藏的力量，那么作为群体、作为社区、作为部落，

sentences.en: we are going to have even more influence.
sentences.zh: 我们将产生更大的影响力。

sentences.en: The force we collectively exert can be nearly impossible for any one person to overcome.
sentences.zh: 我们共同施加的力量，几乎可以让任何个人都无法抗拒。

sentences.en: This can explain good things, like the social norms that hold communities together.
sentences.zh: 这可以解释许多美好的事物，比如将社区凝聚在一起的社会规范。

sentences.en: But it can also lead to terrible things.
sentences.zh: 但它也可能导致可怕的后果。

sentences.en: When we are part of a mob, the effects can be monstrous.
sentences.zh: 当我们成为暴民的一部分时，其影响可能是极其可怕的。
